body.html: Ing Oun Guesthouse — known in Thai as Baan Ingoon Guesthouse — has been open since 2012 as a budget 2-star guesthouse on Phanom Phanarak Road in That Phanom, Nakhon Phanom · What sets it apart from the usual hundred-baht stays is that the building is a French-Indochinese shophouse that has been carefully restored — old plaster, a varnished wooden staircase, and louvre shutters that still hold the feel of an earlier era · It's a small place with just a few rooms, so it feels quiet and private, more like staying in a friend's home than a hotel.

Location is the main reason people choose it · The guesthouse sits in the heart of old That Phanom, just one block from the Mekong and about a 5-minute walk from Phra That Phanom, the revered stupa most visitors come to see · Around the property you'll find the That Phanom morning market, local eateries and small cafés, all within walking distance · That means you can wake up, walk the market, pay respects at the Phra That and stroll back without ever needing a car.
"Such a beautiful old building, the room was small but clean, the owner was kind, and it's only a few minutes' walk to Phra That Phanom — far better value than expected."

The rooms here are small and simply done, but clean and comfortable · Each comes with air conditioning, a firm bed with good-quality linens, a wall-mounted flat-screen TV, a mini-fridge and an en-suite wet bathroom with hot water · The room many guests ask for is one of the front rooms, with wooden louvre shutters and a small balcony over the street — open them up and you get the full old-town atmosphere · Downstairs there's a relaxed sitting area where breakfast is served · Facilities are kept simple in line with a guesthouse: free Wi-Fi, parking, room service, and an airport transfer on request.

Because it's a small guesthouse in an old building, the thing to understand before booking is that rooms are compact and there are only a few of them · If you want a spacious room or full hotel facilities, this may not be the right fit · The building is genuinely old, so it shows some age in places, and the upper floor is reached by a wooden staircase with no lift · Breakfast and the airport transfer are best confirmed when you book, as this is a small, owner-run place where the front desk may not be staffed 24 hours — if you arrive late, give your time in advance.

One more thing to know: the guesthouse is in That Phanom, not in Nakhon Phanom town, which is about 50 km away · If your plans centre on Nakhon Phanom city — the Mekong Walking Street or the Phaya Si Sattanakharat naga statue — staying in That Phanom is a bit far · But if your main goal is to visit Phra That Phanom, soak up the old riverside town and live at a slow, local pace, Ing Oun's location is an advantage you won't get from a hotel in the city.

The verdict from real guest reviews: Ing Oun Guesthouse is best for travellers who want to stay near Phra That Phanom in somewhere with character, at a budget price · It suits couples, solo travellers and backpackers who enjoy old-town atmosphere on a tight budget more than those who want a large room or full facilities · If you can accept a small room in an old, owner-run building, it's one of the most bookable options for a night in That Phanom.

A tip from following Nakhon Phanom stays: ask for a front room with the wooden shutters and balcony for the fullest old-town feel · During the Phra That Phanom homage festival (around February–March) crowds pour into That Phanom — rooms near the stupa fill fast and rates climb — so if you're coming then, book several weeks ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate first.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Ing Oun Guesthouse (Baan Ingoon) Nakhon Phanom

faq.q: Where is Ing Oun Guesthouse, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The guesthouse is at 19 Moo 11 Phanom Phanarak Road, That Phanom, Nakhon Phanom · It's about a 5-minute walk from Phra That Phanom and one block from the Mekong · The That Phanom morning market and local eateries are within walking distance · It's in That Phanom district, about 50 km from Nakhon Phanom town.

faq.q: How much does Ing Oun Guesthouse cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 550/night for a Standard Room · There are air-con rooms and front rooms with a wooden-shutter balcony for a little more · Prices depend on the season and package and rise during the Phra That festival, so compare several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Ing Oun Guesthouse best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers who want to stay near Phra That Phanom in somewhere with character, at a budget price · Good for couples, solo travellers or backpackers who enjoy old-town atmosphere on a tight budget over a large room or full facilities.

faq.q: What should I know before booking Ing Oun Guesthouse?
faq.a: It's a small guesthouse in a restored old building · Rooms are compact, there are only a few of them, and there's no lift — the upper floor is up a wooden staircase · The front desk may not be 24-hour, so give your check-in time in advance for late arrivals · An airport transfer is available but should be arranged ahead.

faq.q: Is Ing Oun Guesthouse in Nakhon Phanom town?
faq.a: No · The guesthouse is in That Phanom district, about 50 km from Nakhon Phanom town · If your main goal is to visit Phra That Phanom and explore the old riverside town, this location is ideal · But if you want to be in Nakhon Phanom city — the Mekong Walking Street or the Phaya Si Sattanakharat statue — choose a hotel in the town instead.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: In normal periods, 1–2 weeks ahead is usually enough, as the guesthouse has only a few rooms · But during the Phra That Phanom homage festival (around February–March) the town is packed and rooms near the stupa fill fast with higher rates, so book several weeks ahead · Choose a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm yet.
